name: WebTAK-Plugin-Channels
description: Channel and group management plugin for WebTAK in the ILWG CAP / VISTA stack. Browse, join, and manage TAK channels directly from the WebTAK map interface.
highlight: Brings multi-channel coordination to WebTAK dispatchers during ILWG activations.

name: WebTAK-Plugin-VideoViewer
description: Floating, resizable video windows for RTSP/RTSPS/SRT/RTMP/HLS feeds layered over the WebTAK map. Routes all streams through TAK Restreamer (MediaMTX) as HLS or WebRTC WHEP. Built for the ILWG CAP / VISTA stack.
highlight: Live camera feeds from MediaMTX directly overlaid on the WebTAK common operating picture.

name: ATAK-Plugin-QuickCapture
description: Quick feature capture and sync to ArcGIS feature services from ATAK. QR-code project templates, photo attachments, CalTopo integration, and bidirectional ArcGIS sync with offline support.
highlight: Field teams capture and upload geo-features directly to ArcGIS with no desktop workflow.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-FeatureLink
description: Bidirectional bridge between Esri ArcGIS Feature Services and the TAK ecosystem. Pushes CoT to ArcGIS feature layers, writes PLI tracks back from feature layers to TAK. Full platform coverage: ATAK 5.6/5.7, WinTAK 5.6/5.7, CloudTAK, and TAK Portal.
highlight: One feature service, visible and editable from ATAK, WinTAK, CloudTAK, and ArcGIS simultaneously — no manual sync.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-Aleph
description: Draw a search area on any TAK client and receive an offline data package (imagery, DTED elevation, OSM street data) back as a mission package. Python service handles tile fetching and package assembly; ATAK, WinTAK, CloudTAK, and infra-TAK clients included.
highlight: Pre-loaded offline map tiles for a mission AO in one draw operation — no GIS desk or desktop tool required.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-CrowdCAD
description: Crowd-sourced CAD bridge + ATAK/CloudTAK/WinTAK/WebTAK clients for event dispatch. Built for IU football medical operations — responders on ATAK, dispatchers on WinTAK and CloudTAK, CoT-linked.
highlight: Operational at IU home games — ATAK-equipped medical responders dispatched live from the TAK COP.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-WMD_Plotter
description: ATAK and WinTAK plugins for WMD Plotter, a browser-based CBRN hazard modeling tool. Fetches the live KML hazard overlay — chemical plume, blast, radiation/RDD, BLEVE, dense gas, fire/smoke — and renders it directly on the TAK map with auto-refresh.
highlight: CBRN hazard zones from WMD Plotter rendered live on the TAK COP — chemical plume and blast radius without manual file import.

name: TAK-Plugin-UI-Builder
description: Drag-and-drop visual designer for ATAK plugin layouts. Generates valid Java/XML for DropDownReceiver dialogs and panels. No build step — deployed as a static GitHub Pages app.
highlight: Live at jpat-12.github.io/TAK-Plugin-UI-Builder — zero-install dev tool for the TAK community.

name: CloudTAK-Plugin_Development
description: Practical guide, API reference, and copy-paste scaffold for building CloudTAK plugins. Covers the web plugin (Vue 3 / TypeScript) and server route halves, verified against CloudTAK 13.14.1. Includes version-drift guidance.
highlight: The reverse-engineered CloudTAK plugin contract in one repo — docs, working template, and API reference.

name: TAK-PluginSuite-ATAK_ICU
description: ATAK 5.6 plugin reverse-engineered from ICU and uastool APKs. Turns an Android phone into a UAS ground control station integrated with the TAK common operating picture.
highlight: Bridges phone-as-UAS-platform into the TAK COP without proprietary hardware or vendor lock-in.

name: WinTAK_Plugin-ImageFolderSync
description: WinTAK plugin that watches a folder for GPS-tagged photos and automatically plots them as map markers. Supports broadcast, targeted contacts, and DataSync mission feeds — with attachment links in the marker popup.
highlight: GPS-tagged drone or field camera photos appear on the TAK map as soon as they land in the watched folder.

name: TAKPortal-Plugin-HostedATAKPlugins
description: Shell installer that patches a TAK Portal checkout in-place to serve hosted ATAK plugins directly from the portal. Operators scan and install plugins from within ATAK without sideloading APKs.
highlight: One-command patch makes TAK Portal a full plugin distribution hub — no sideloading, no manual APK transfer.

name: InfraTAK-Plugin-TAKRestreamerQRCodes
description: infra-TAK plugin that generates QR codes for TAK Restreamer (MediaMTX) stream endpoints. Scan to connect field devices to live streams without typing URLs.
highlight: One QR scan puts a field device on the right MediaMTX stream path — no URL memorization.

name: InfraTAK-Module-MigrateAuthentik
description: infra-TAK module for migrating Authentik SSO configurations between versions or instances. Automates the transition of authentication flows, users, groups, and applications.
highlight: Automates the painful Authentik migration process for TAK infrastructure operators upgrading SSO stacks.

name: TeamAwearnessKit-Esri-Integration
description: Early Node-RED bridge connecting Survey123 form submissions to CoT markers on TAK, and CoT position tracks back to ArcGIS Online feature layers. The bidirectional Esri ↔ TAK closed loop that preceded FeatureLink.
highlight: Proved the Survey123 → TAK → ArcGIS closed loop before the full FeatureLink suite existed.

name: TeamAwearnessKit
description: Early TAK resource kit with custom icons, map overlays, standard operating procedures, and a user registration interface. The precursor to the TeamAwarenessKit Esri Integration work.
highlight: Original HTML resource collection that seeded the TeamAwarenessKit Esri integration and icon library work.
